Alerts and the Athan

On this page
  • Set up the alerts
  • Choose a sound
  • Add your own sound
  • When the phone does not allow alerts
  • What happens when an alert comes
  • Keep the alerts coming

Taqwim can alert you at the time of each prayer, play the Athan, and remind you a few minutes before. Alerts are on by default.

Alerts work on Android, iPhone and iPad. On Windows, macOS, Linux and the web, the Alerts tab says "Notifications work on Android and iPhone; they do not reach this device yet". You can still set your choices there.

Set up the alerts

  1. Open Settings (the sliders button in the top bar).
  2. Tap the Alerts tab.
  3. Make sure Turn on notifications is on. Turning it on asks the phone for any permission still missing.
  4. Under each prayer, choose what you want (see below). Every change is saved at once.

Each of Fajr, Sunrise, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha has its own group:

RowWhat it doesDefault
At the time (the switch beside the prayer's name)An alert when the time beginsOn for the five prayers, off for Sunrise
SoundWhat the alert playsThe Athan takbirs for the five prayers, the device tone for Sunrise
Reminder beforeA second alert None, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 45 or 60 minutes beforeNone
Reminder soundWhat the reminder plays (shown once a reminder is set)Device tone
VibrateVibrate with the alert and the reminderOn

Sunrise is not a prayer, so its alert is off by default. Turn it on if you want to know when Fajr's time ends.

Choose a sound

Each Sound and Reminder sound list offers:

  • Device tone: the phone's own notification sound;
  • Silent: no sound; with Vibrate on, the alert only vibrates;
  • Athan takbirs (short) – Sheikh Abdullah Al-Zaylai: the opening takbirs of the Athan, about 33 seconds;
  • Full Athan – Sheikh Abdullah Al-Zaylai: the whole Athan, about four minutes;
  • any sound you added yourself.

Under App sounds, each built-in sound has:

  • Play, to listen to it (the button reads Stop while it plays);
  • Use for all, to set it at the time of all five prayers at once.

Add your own sound

  1. Under Your sounds, tap Add a sound.
  2. Choose a WAV or MP3 file of up to 10 MB.
  3. Taqwim asks "Use it at the time of all five prayers?". Tap Use for all, or Not now to choose it prayer by prayer later.

Each of your sounds has Play, Use for all and Delete. Deleting a sound sets every alert that used it back to the device tone.

On iPhone and iPad, an alert plays only the first 30 seconds of its sound; this is a limit of iOS. The full Athan therefore plays in full on Android only.

The web version cannot add or play sounds: it shows "Adding sounds is not available in the web version".

When the phone does not allow alerts

If something blocks the alerts, the Alerts tab says so, with an Allow button:

  • "Notifications are off for this app in the phone's settings": tap Allow, or turn notifications on for Taqwim in the phone's settings.
  • "Alerts may come a few minutes late: allow the app to set exact alarms" (Android): tap Allow and switch on Alarms & reminders (the name varies by phone) for Taqwim.

See also Troubleshooting for battery settings on Android.

What happens when an alert comes

On Android

  • The alert sounds at the prayer's minute and shows a notification with a Stop button. The sound plays to its end, so a full Athan plays completely.
  • The sound uses the alarm volume of the phone.
  • If you open Taqwim while the sound plays, a banner at the top says Alert sound playing: with the prayer's name and a stop button.
  • Only one sound plays at a time: an alert that arrives while another one plays stops it and stays silent.
  • If the phone delivers an alert more than 10 minutes late (for example after deep sleep or battery saving), it does not sound. It leaves a silent notification that still names the prayer and its time.
  • After the phone restarts, Taqwim sets its alarms again by itself.

On iPhone and iPad

  • iOS plays the sound itself, for at most 30 seconds, and never two at once.
  • Vibration follows the phone's own sound and haptics settings.
  • Taqwim cannot stop a sound that iOS is playing, so the in-app stop banner appears on Android only.

Keep the alerts coming

Taqwim sets the coming alerts on the phone, up to 60 at a time, every time you open it and whenever you change the place, the method or the alert settings. With five alerts a day this covers about twelve days; with reminders on, fewer.

Open Taqwim at least once a week so the list of alerts stays filled.
